rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING FORFEITURES ON THE OVERHEAD CHARGES DUE TO UNINTENDED OR UNANNOUNCED UTILITY SERVICE INTERRUPTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to compensate consumers or subscribers for the inconvenience and reduced productivity brought by electricity outages, water, and internet connectivity interruptions; Excludes services interruptions due to, but not limited to force majeure, acts of God, insurrection, rebellion, negligence by the subscriber, from the forfeitures as provided for in this Act.

Seeks to charge a minute-based forfeiture on the fixed or overhead costs on utility bills from the time of unintended or unannounced interruptions until the restoration of the utility service.

Mandates the Energy Regulatory Commission, Local Water Administration, and National Telecommunications Commission to determine forfeiture rates and overhead or fixed charges.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE SECURING MANUFACTURING REVITALIZATION AND TRANSFORMATION (SMaRT) PROGRAM IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to revitalize and transform the country´s manufacturing sector into the Fourth Industrial Revolution to make them more globally competitive, through the:  development of new production techniques and business models; performance-based, targeted, time-bound, and transparent fiscal and non-fiscal support; stimulate innovation, expand research and development, and accelerate research commercialization activities, attract investments in emerging industries and industry clusters, and encourage global value chain upgrading.

Defines “Global Value Chain” as global geographic fragmentation of activities involved in the production, supply, distribution, and post-sale activities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to foster and protect Filipino creativity and innovation in a highly competitive borderless world through the protection of IP Rights, to secure quality, reliable and safe products, and genuine and authentic music, works of arts, and literature.

Seeks to create an enabling environment that will promote and steer creativity, innovation, and development of large companies and the micro, small and medium enterprises, including start-ups; Intends to deter counterfeiting and piracy in the physical and online markets; Proposes to take down or block websites and online posts that advertise, sell or offer to sell, promote, and influence consumers to patronize counterfeit products; infringement or download pirated music, movies, and other materials.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REVISED CONSUMER ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms, among others: Chain Distribution Plans or Pseudo Investment, Ponzi Scheme, Telemarketing, Open-End-Credit Plan, Stockpiling, Counterfeit Products, Trademark, etc.
Proposes several provisions, among others, to update and improve Republic Act No.7394 to keep up with the changing times - the age of technology:  a) Basic Consumer Rights, b) Products Standards, Technical Regulations, and Conformity Assessment, c) Production, Sale, Distribution, Advertising, and Promotion of Health Products, d) Protection Against Hazardous Substances, e) Protection Against Deceptive, Unfair and Unconscionable Sales Acts and Practices, f) Regulation of Practices Relative to Weights and Measures, g) Sale of Products with Warranty, h) Labeling and Fair Packaging, i) Liability for Product and Services, j) Advertising and Sales Promotion, k) Regulation of Repair Service Terms, and l) Consumer Credit Transaction.
Seeks to establish the Philippine Online Dispute Resolution and the Consumer Affairs Council, and provides for the Consumer Welfare and Protection Education Program.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL MECHANISMS TO ACCELERATE THE RECOVERY AND BOLSTER THE RESILIENCY OF THE PHILIPPINE ECONOMY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: \" Bayanihan To Arise As One Act.\"
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide additional economic stimulus package to help the government to recover from the adverse impact of the COVID-19 pandemic .

Proposes to allocate 108 billion pesos for additional social amelioration to impacted households, 100 billion pesos for capacity building to impacted sectors, 52 billion pesos for wage subsidies, 70 billion pesos for capacity building for agricultural producers, 30 billion pesos for allowances to students and teachers, 30 billion pesos for assistance to displaced workers, 25 billion pesos for COVID-19 treatment and vaccines, and 5 billion pesos for the rehabilitation of typhoon-affected areas.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09411

rows.author: G097
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPEDITING THE PURCHASE AND ADMINISTRATION OF VACCINES FOR THE PROTECTION AGAINST THE CORONAVIRUS DISEASE 2019 BY PROVIDING EXEMPTIONS TO COMPLIANCE WITH THE PROCUREMENT REQUIREMENTS UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9184, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "GOVERNMENT PROCUREMENT REFORM ACT", AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to ensure that the COVID-19 vaccine is procured and administered in an expeditious, effective, efficient, and equitable manner.

Authorizes the Local Government Units to directly purchase Covid-19 vaccines and secure other goods and services necessary for their storage, transport, distribution, and administration notwithstanding the provisions of RA No. 9184, or the “Government Procurement Reform Act,” Section 338 of Republic Act No. 7160, as amended, or the “Local Government Code of 1991,” and Section 88 of PD No. 1445, as amended, or the “Government Auditing Code of the Philippines.” 

Creates the Indemnification Fund which shall cover the Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) to ensure the safety of individuals who will receive vaccination from COVID-19.

Exempts the procurement, importation, storage, transport, distribution, and administration of the Covid-19 vaccines by the local government units from customs duties, value-added tax, excise tax, and other fees, provided, that the vaccines acquired shall only be used for their residents and constituents, and not for commercial distribution.
rows.status: Republic Act RA11525 enacted on 2021-02-26

rows.author: H053
rows.title_full:
AN ACT 
PROVIDING FOR THE REVISED WAREHOUSE RECEIPTS LAW OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Revised Warehouse Receipts Law Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish a simplified, unified, and modern framework for the storage of goods in warehouses and the subsequent trading of interest therein.

Proposes to establish a central electronic Registry for all warehouse receipts which will be made readily available online and eventually integrated with other existing Registries.

Enables the agricultural sector to convert goods and products into credit in a faster and simpler way, promote economic activity by increasing access, particularly for entities engaged in agricultural businesses such as farming, to least cost credit.

Provides for the following provisions: 1.) Obligations and rights of warehouse operators upon their receipts; 2.) Negotiation and transfer of receipt; and 3.) Criminal Offenses, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2021-03-09, transmitted to the Senate on 2021-03-10 and received by the Senate on 2021-03-10
